name_orig: Innocentius III (Lotharius de Segni / Lotario dei Conti)
role_place: Pope 1198-1216 (Rome, Lateran); convened the Fourth Lateran Council (1215).
why_relevant: His crusade bull Quia maior (April 1213) calls Muhammad a 'perditionis filius' and 'pseudopropheta' and says he seduced many with worldly enticements and carnal pleasures.
fame: Known mainly as a pope who shaped crusade policy and the Fourth Lateran Council; his Islam remarks are brief and mostly rhetorical, found in a crusade appeal, not in a theological treatise. Fame of the Muhammad sentence not verified (see passages.json, famous field).
catholic_status: Pope (no canonization known to me; not verified in a source I read)

role_place: Humanist and diplomat; pope 1458-1464 (Rome); called for a crusade at the Congress of Mantua (1459).
why_relevant: His Epistola ad Mahumetem (c. 1461), a long open letter to Sultan Mehmed II, refutes Muhammad's claims, the Qur'an's miracles, paradise and its doctrine of angels, and defends the Trinity and Incarnation.
fame: A famous humanist-pope; the Epistola ad Mahumetem circulated in many 15th-century printings (archive.org copies of 1474 and 1477 read; catalogue snippets also list Cologne c. 1469-72 and Rome 1490/91) and is studied in modern scholarship (Toffanin 1953, Baca 1990, per search snippets). Its citation by later Catholic or Protestant authors was not verified.
catholic_status: Pope (not canonized; not verified in a source I read)
